title: o_measure.py: shadow-calibrated cohort novelty plus replacement, the O statistic that separates a moving landscape from Hash Chemistry's finite adaptive walk
summary: Importable module for C:open-ended claims. Given a replication log (t, kind) or a list of censuses ({kind: count}), it counts kinds BORN in each window whose activity within Lc of birth reaches a*, with a* the 99.9th percentile of the same early activity in a neutral reference: an in-world neutral twin, or the Rechtsteiner-Bedau shadow that rb_shadow (kind-level births, innovations, deaths; random parents and victims) or census_shadow builds from the run itself. It also reports replacement (top-k overlap with the first and previous windows). Self-test on a synthetic Moran process (N=500, 8000 steps, Lc=win=1000): late significant new kinds neutral 4 and 0 against 8 shadows 0-2; recurrent sweeps (s=0.2 per new mutant) 15 and 14 against the same envelopes. Calibrated in the parent findings: Sayama's Hash Chemistry freezes (0-1 late significant kinds vs shadow 3-39 in 7/8 runs), a moving landscape passes (1450-1764 vs 18-30), evoloop is bounded.

tool.usage: import o_measure as om; st, sk = om.rb_shadow(birth_t, innov, death_t, n0=initial_kinds); r = om.report(t, k, st, sk, T, Lc=1000, win=1000); O needs r['late_sig'] above the shadow envelope (run 5-10 shadow seeds) AND r['top_first'] decaying, in late windows
tool.caveats: Use several shadow replicates for an envelope; one shadow is noisy at small counts. Give rb_shadow the real initial kinds. a* depends on Lc; choose Lc around a sweep time. A fixed a* (not calibrated) is passed by drift in fast-replicating worlds (complex hash world: neutral twin 2800-3600 per window at a*=50). Kinds must be heritable units the world copies (genotypes, compositions), not threshold blobs.
